intro: Lesson 39. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا (٩) وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًۭا (١٠) وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلنَّهَارَ مَعَاشًۭا (١١) وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًۭا شِدَادًۭا (١٢) وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًۭا وَهَّاجًۭا (١٣) وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ مَآءًۭ ثَجَّاجًۭا (١٤) لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِۦ حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا (١٥) وَجَنَّٰتٍ أَلْفَافًا (١٦)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And made your sleep [a means for] rest
And made the night as clothing
And made the day for livelihood
And constructed above you seven strong [heavens]
And sent down, from the rain clouds, pouring water
That We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation

questions.q: Chunk and link An-Naba' 78:9-16 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 78:9-16 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 78:9-16 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
Sleep for rest, night as clothing, day for living, seven strong heavens, the sun, rain for grain, plants and gardens.

questions.q: Link 78:14 to the water cycle: what are 'the rain clouds' doing?
questions.a: Clouds hold water vapour that condenses and falls as heavy rain.
A) The sun. Allah made the sun a blazing lamp.

questions.q: Think again: Sleep, night, day, rain, crops: An-Naba' lists daily blessings. Which one would you miss most if it stopped tomorrow?
questions.a: Each pupil chooses; the point of 78:9 to 16 is that every one is a gift and a sign.
